findings.title: safe_urlopen exception not caught in OAuthLoginView
findings.body: The `safe_urlopen(url=ghip.get_oauth_access_token_url(), data=data)` call at line 423 sits outside the `try`/`except Exception` block at lines 425-429. If `safe_urlopen` raises (e.g. DNS failure, connection refused, TLS error, or any non-success path where it does not return a response object), the exception propagates up and the user gets a 500 instead of the intended "Invalid installation request." page. The current try/except only guards `safe_urlread`, `decode`, and `parse_qsl`. Move `safe_urlopen` inside the `try` block so all failure paths return `error(request, self.active_organization)`.

findings.title: get_user_info exception not handled
findings.body: `get_user_info(payload["access_token"])` at line 434 is not wrapped in any exception handler. If the GitHub `/user` call raises (network error, non-2xx that the helper propagates, malformed JSON, missing keys, etc.), the exception bubbles up and the user sees a 500 error rather than the documented "Invalid installation request." failure page. Wrap the call so any exception results in the same `error(request, self.active_organization)` return path used for the other failure cases.

findings.title: User-mismatch check bypassed when Integration record is not yet present
findings.body: In `GitHubInstallation.dispatch`, the `except Integration.DoesNotExist:` branch at lines 479-481 returns `pipeline.next_step()` immediately, so the new OAuth-authenticated-user vs. sender check at lines 501-505 is never executed. GitHub's install webhook and the user redirect are independent, so when the redirect arrives before the webhook (or the webhook is delayed/retried), the `Integration` row does not exist yet, this branch is taken, and the pipeline proceeds to `build_integration`, which creates the `OrganizationIntegration` for the attacker's installation linked to the victim's Sentry org with no sender comparison. The whole purpose of this PR (validating the GitHub user that authorised the app with the user that installed it) is defeated in that race window. The check should be enforced (e.g. wait/retry for the Integration record and require `metadata["sender"]["login"]` before continuing) instead of silently advancing.

findings.title: test_installation_not_found no longer exercises the installation-not-found path
findings.body: The rewritten `test_installation_not_found` (line 379) issues its OAuth callback with `state="ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05"` (line 392), which does not match the pipeline signature `"9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3"`. As a result the test bails out in `OAuthLoginView` with the state-mismatch error and never reaches `GitHubInstallation.dispatch` / `build_integration`, where the `IntegrationError("The GitHub installation could not be found.")` is raised. The 404 stub on `/app/installations/{id}` is therefore never exercised, and after this PR there is no test covering the actual installation-not-found failure path. The second GET should use the correct pipeline-signature state so the OAuth step succeeds and the code path under test is actually hit.

findings.title: OAuth authorize URL built with f-string instead of urlencode
findings.body: The redirect at line 408 (`f"{...}?client_id={github_client_id}&state={state}&redirect_uri={redirect_uri}"`) concatenates query parameters with raw f-string interpolation instead of `urlencode`. `pipeline.signature`, the GitHub OAuth `client_id`, and the absolute `redirect_uri` could in principle contain reserved characters (`&`, `=`, `#`, `+`, spaces, unicode). Any such character would either be misinterpreted by GitHub (silently corrupting `state` or `redirect_uri`) or be used to tamper with the query string. Use `urlencode` (or `urllib.parse.urlencode`) to construct the query parameters, matching the safer practice used elsewhere in the file.
